grounded_facts: A high-tension meeting between Winter and Amy in which he interrogates her, reveals cryptic truths, and asserts psychological dominance.
memories.memory_text: I interrogated Amy, pressing her with questions that made her uneasy, asserting my control over the conversation and the space between us, making it clear she couldn't just walk away.

grounded_facts: Winter runs his fingers over and between Amy's, enumerating anatomical parts while questioning what constitutes reality and identity.
memories.memory_text: I ran my fingers between hers, continuing to enumerate the components of her hand while questioning what constitutes reality and identity, feeling her freeze as I demonstrated how easily certainty can unravel.

grounded_facts: Winter uses a metaphor of negative space to diminish Amy Klein's significance, framing her as an insignificant remnant.
memories.memory_text: I used the metaphor of negative space to show how Amy Klein is just a tiny remnant left after subtracting all the possibilities that could have been, making her significance vanish in comparison.

grounded_facts: Winter articulates a nihilistic worldview, describing physical presence as an absence and asserting that humans are less than nothing.

memories.memory_text: I spoke the truth about existence, telling Amy that physical presence is not real—it's an absence, and we are less than nothing in every essential way, to show her how hollow reality truly is.

grounded_facts: Amy begins to psychologically yield to Winter's ideology during his monologue.

memories.memory_text: I led the ritual in the dungeon, standing over Amy as she woke, placing the puzzle box on the altar, and beginning the initiation.

grounded_facts: Winter presents a knife to Amy as a 'gift' promising freedom from fear and pain, framed as a coercive invitation to join the Deaders.

memories.memory_text: I saw Amy panic and fight back when the Deaders grabbed her, shouting 'No!' and trying to break free from their grasp.

memories.memory_text: I heard Marla say that fear is where you go to learn, and then she told Amy there's no turning back without someone bringing her back—making me wonder if she meant me all along.

grounded_facts: A tense nighttime walk through a distorted subway tunnel where Marla imparts key ideological and personal revelations to Amy while moving toward an unknown destination.

grounded_facts: Winter appears dramatically as a train approaches, calling out to Amy with the phrase 'All roads lead home,' halting the forward momentum of the scene and redirecting Amy's attention.

grounded_facts: Winter appears as a savior figure, calling Amy by name and declaring 'All roads lead home,' asserting his control and offering emotional resolution.
memories.memory_text: I called out to Amy, arms open, and told her 'All roads lead home'—I could see her turn to me, away from the train, and I knew I was guiding her back where she belonged.

grounded_facts: Amy encounters Marla in the psych ward, who cryptically reveals that Amy is the chosen one destined to solve the puzzle Winter seeks, warning her of limited time and the necessity of facing inner truths.
memories.memory_text: I overheard Marla in the psych ward talking about me—how Winter can't solve the puzzle himself, and that only someone like me, with the right darkness inside, could be the one he's been searching for. She said I'm the chosen one, that Winter needs me to come back, and that I have to face him to make it out, but I don't know if I can trust what she told me.

grounded_facts: Pinhead has Winter torn apart by hooks and chains as punishment for claiming ownership of the puzzle box.

memories.memory_text: I witnessed Amy stab herself in the chest with the knife, choosing to deny her soul to Pinhead.

grounded_facts: Amy activates a tape recorder to document the events at the crack den.
memories.memory_text: I reached into my coat pocket, took out my tape recorder, clicked it on, and put it back to start recording everything.

grounded_facts: Amy pretends to ingest X by allowing it on her tongue, then secretly discards it.
memories.memory_text: I let the man place the pill on my tongue and pretended to swallow it, but I secretly took it out and flicked it away.

grounded_facts: A drug-fueled gathering involving crack and X, used by Amy Klein for undercover observation.
memories.memory_text: I moved through the party, pretending to take X and acting high while secretly staying alert to observe everyone around me.

grounded_facts: Amy pretends to be under the influence while observing others.
memories.memory_text: I pretended to be under the influence by taking the crack pipe and quickly passing it on, all while keeping a sharp eye on the other partygoers as if I were a reporter gathering information.

grounded_facts: The Man gives Amy a drug, testing her participation in the party.
memories.memory_text: I think he gave me the drug to test if I'd go along with the party, so I pretended to be under the influence while watching the others closely.

grounded_facts: Amy experiences blurred vision, suggesting she may have been slipped a substance.
memories.memory_text: I noticed my vision starting to blur, and I wondered if he had slipped something into my drink.

grounded_facts: The Man pulls Amy onto the bed and begins undressing her against her will.
memories.memory_text: I was pulled onto the bed by him and couldn't fight back as he started undressing me.

grounded_facts: After the party, The Man tries to pull Amy close and becomes rough when she resists.
After the party, Amy is alone with The Man who becomes physically aggressive.
memories.memory_text: I was alone with The Man after the party ended, and when I tried to find a way out, he grabbed me and got rough—I couldn’t fight him off as he pulled me onto the bed and started undressing me.

grounded_facts: The Man attempts to assault Amy but loses consciousness before completing the act.
memories.memory_text: I saw him lose consciousness before he could finish what he started, but I was still trapped and scared.

grounded_facts: Amy's vision swirls and she collapses out of frame, likely due to intoxication or drugging.
memories.memory_text: I felt the room start to swirl around me, and I couldn't hold my balance—I collapsed out of frame, unsure if it was from intoxication or something worse.

grounded_facts: Amy regains consciousness and quickly evaluates her environment upon waking in an unfamiliar place.
memories.memory_text: I opened my eyes and quickly looked around, trying to make sense of where I was.

grounded_facts: Amy checks herself and feels relief upon realizing her clothes are intact.
memories.memory_text: I checked myself and felt relief when I realized I was still dressed.

grounded_facts: Amy retrieves a small tape recorder from the floor and rewinds it, indicating its importance.
memories.memory_text: I picked up my small tape recorder from the floor and rewound it before putting it away.

grounded_facts: Amy takes a half-empty pack of cigarettes and exits the crack den.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed a half-empty pack of cigarettes and slipped out of the crack den quietly.

grounded_facts: After being taunted about her 'crack whore' article, Amy responds by flipping off the Young Reporter without stopping.
memories.memory_text: As I passed the Young Reporter, he mocked me about my 'crack whore' article, so I flipped him off without breaking stride — he didn't deserve a real response.

grounded_facts: Amy enters the office well after morning hours, showing habitual disregard for punctuality.
memories.memory_text: I walked into the office late, and I could feel people giving me dirty looks, but I didn't care — Betty even called out that it was half past four, like I should be ashamed.

grounded_facts: Charles uses sarcasm and sensory description to mock Amy's entrance, referencing her smell and past employment issues.
memories.memory_text: I walked into the office and Charles immediately mocked me with that sarcastic tone, making some snide comment about how he could smell me coming—something about sweat and patchouli—like he always does to get under my skin.

grounded_facts: Charles asks Amy if she has heard of the Deaders, testing her knowledge of underground subcultures.
memories.memory_text: Charles asked me if I’d ever heard of a group called the Deaders, spelling it out like I was supposed to know, but I told him straight—no, I’d never heard of them.

grounded_facts: On the videotape, Katya participates in a ritual where she declares her unreality and lies down with a gun to her head, suggesting a dangerous psychological or physical test.
memories.memory_text: I sat forward, not quite believing what I was seeing on the tape—Katya declaring she wasn't real and lying down with a gun to her head. It looked like some kind of dangerous initiation.

grounded_facts: Amy initially misunderstands 'Deaders' as 'Deadheads', but after watching the tape, she is confronted with a disturbing ritual performed by a group calling themselves the Deaders.
memories.memory_text: I thought Charles was talking about Deadheads at first—those Grateful Dead fans in their forties who still idolize Jerry Garcia—so I told him what I knew, but then he corrected me, spelling out 'Deaders' like it was something else entirely. When I said I'd never heard of them, he told me to watch the tape. I sat there, smoking, and saw this disturbing ritual: a woman named Marla introduced Katya and then Winter, who called himself the leader, asked someone if they joined the Deaders of their own free will. I leaned forward, not sure if what I was seeing was real, but it felt wrong in a way I couldn't ignore.

grounded_facts: Charles and Amy watch a disturbing videotape sent anonymously, showing a cult initiation ritual conducted by a group called the Deaders.
memories.memory_text: I watched the videotape with Charles, and I couldn't look away — I sat forward, stunned by what I was seeing, some kind of cult initiation that felt too real to dismiss.

grounded_facts: A ritual is conducted in a dingy apartment where Katya is initiated into the Deaders by lying down with a loaded gun to her head while repeating that she is not real.
memories.memory_text: I saw a ritual on the tape — a girl named Katya lying naked on a mattress with a loaded gun to her head, repeating that she wasn't real, and I'm not sure if it was real or some twisted performance, but it shook me.

grounded_facts: Charles reveals a recently received videotape depicting a cult-like group called the Deaders, initiating a new member in a ritual involving a gun.
memories.memory_text: I watched the tape Charles showed me—it was some disturbing footage of a cult called the Deaders initiating a new member, with a man named Winter putting a gun to her head, and I couldn't look away.

grounded_facts: Amy urgently asks Charles if he has reported the tape to the police, expressing moral distress.
memories.memory_text: I urgently asked Charles if he had called the police about the tape because I was disturbed by what I'd seen and needed to know if it was being treated as a real crime.

grounded_facts: Charles suggests the tape might be real and dares Amy to investigate it seriously, framing it as a journalistic opportunity.
memories.memory_text: Charles looked at me and suggested the tape might be real, daring me to take it seriously as a journalistic opportunity instead of dismissing it as just some fake horror footage.

grounded_facts: Amy unconsciously touches her own head, replicating Katya's gesture of inserting fingers into the head wound, indicating psychological impact.
memories.memory_text: I didn't realize I was touching the side of my head with my fingers, just like Katya did in the footage, but I must have been affected more deeply than I thought.

grounded_facts: Charles recounts his father's remark about fortune-tellers, linking it to the idea of power through knowledge of the future.
memories.memory_text: I remember Charles telling me about his father’s remark on fortune-tellers—that if someone could really see the future, they wouldn’t be stuck in a rundown storefront but would own the earth.

grounded_facts: After watching the tape, Charles provides Amy with travel documents and funding to go to Bucharest, the return address on the mysterious tape's envelope, and Amy accepts the assignment to investigate the Deaders cult.
memories.memory_text: After I watched the tape, Charles handed me travel documents and funding for a trip to Bucharest—the return address on the envelope—and I accepted the assignment to investigate the Deaders cult.

grounded_facts: Amy exits a cab and approaches the front door of an apartment building in Bucharest.
memories.memory_text: I got out of the cab and walked up to the front door of an apartment building in Bucharest.

grounded_facts: Amy retrieves the envelope containing the tape and checks the name 'Marla Chen' against the mailboxes to confirm the location.
memories.memory_text: I pulled the envelope out of my bag and checked the name 'Marla Chen' on it, comparing it to the names on the mailboxes to confirm I was in the right place.

grounded_facts: The Manager confronts Amy about her presence and intentions, expressing suspicion.
memories.memory_text: I was confronted by the Manager, who stared at me like he knew I was up to something, and he asked me, 'Have you lost something?' right after I jumped up when he appeared.

grounded_facts: Amy offers money to the Manager in exchange for temporary access to the room.
memories.memory_text: I pulled out some American bills and offered them to the Manager, telling him I needed five minutes in the room to find what I needed to know.

grounded_facts: After Amy offers money, the Manager unlocks the door and grants her five minutes inside the room.
memories.memory_text: After I gave him the money, I saw the Manager unlock the door and let me in, and I remember him tapping his watch to remind me I only had five minutes inside.

grounded_facts: Upon entering the room, Amy struggles with the overwhelming smell but gradually adjusts her breathing to endure it.
memories.memory_text: I struggled with the overwhelming smell when I entered the room, but I forced myself to adjust by taking slow, deliberate breaths through my nose until I could endure it.

grounded_facts: Amy notices flies emerging from under a door and detects a strong, unpleasant odor, indicating something is wrong inside the room.
memories.memory_text: I saw flies crawling out from under the door, so I knelt down and sniffed, but at first I couldn't tell much. Then I pressed my nose to the bottom of the door and inhaled—the stench was overwhelming, like something rotten. I recoiled and almost vomited, but I made myself breathe through it, taking deeper breaths until I could stand the smell.

grounded_facts: Amy discovers a red photo folder under the bed containing images of a 'deader' party, including one showing Marla next to Winter holding the puzzle box, and another framed through a noose, suggesting symbolic or literal foreshadowing of death.
memories.memory_text: I found a red photo folder under the bed and opened it, seeing pictures from a 'deader' party with Marla in them; one showed her next to Winter holding the puzzle box, and another framed through a noose with her giving a sickly smile, which unsettled me so much that I looked closer, then I stuffed the folder into my satchel when I heard a noise.

grounded_facts: Amy finds Marla's corpse in the bathroom, seated on the toilet with a boot-lace tied around her neck and attached to a wall pipe, indicating suicide by hanging.
memories.memory_text: I saw Marla in the bathroom, sitting on the toilet with a boot-lace tied around her neck and attached to the pipe—I could see how swollen her skin was, and the flies kept buzzing around her as I stepped closer. I covered my mouth because the stench was overwhelming, and I could see one of her hands wasn't visible, with scratches on the floor beneath her fingernails.

grounded_facts: Amy enters Marla's apartment to investigate her disappearance or death, systematically searching rooms and discovering key evidence including photos, the puzzle box, and an envelope addressed to her.
memories.memory_text: I entered Marla's apartment to look for any sign of what happened to her, moving carefully through each room—I checked the kitchen, the bedroom, and found photos showing her with Winter and the puzzle box, then I saw the envelope on the sink with my name on it and I knew I had to take it.

grounded_facts: Amy reaches past Marla's corpse to retrieve a manila envelope labeled 'AMY' from the sink, nearly touching the body, and drops it, requiring her to kneel and retrieve it from behind the corpse.
memories.memory_text: I reached past Marla's corpse to grab the envelope labeled 'AMY' on the sink, nearly touching her body, and when I knocked it down behind her, I had to kneel and reach behind her face to pick it up, my cheek almost brushing the rotting skin.

grounded_facts: Amy forcibly pries open Marla's dead hand to remove the puzzle box, resulting in the snapping of Marla's fingers.
Amy discovers the puzzle box in Marla's concealed hand and forcibly pries her fingers open to take it, causing the blackened fingers to snap.
memories.memory_text: I saw the puzzle box in Marla's hand and pried her fingers open to take it, feeling them snap as I pulled the blackened fingers apart.

grounded_facts: Marla's hand suddenly grabs Amy's leg as she stands beside the body, causing Amy to scream and flee.
After Amy takes the puzzle box, Marla's hand suddenly moves and grabs Amy's leg, causing her to scream and fall backward in terror.
memories.memory_text: I took the puzzle box from Marla's hand, prying her fingers open, and as I stood up, her hand suddenly grabbed my leg—I screamed, fell back, and scrambled away, kicking at her as I fled.

grounded_facts: The manager stops Amy, grabs her arm, and demands to know what she has in her satchel, showing suspicion and authority.
memories.memory_text: I remember the manager stopping me, grabbing my arm, and pointing his cigar at my satchel while demanding to know what I had in it—he looked suspicious and tried to assert authority over me.

grounded_facts: Amy runs into the apartment manager in the hallway, informs him that Marla is dead, and when he demands to know what she has in her satchel, she attacks him after he grabs her arm.
memories.memory_text: I ran into the manager in the hallway, told him Marla was dead—she hung herself—and when he grabbed my arm and demanded to know what was in my satchel, I fought back.

grounded_facts: Amy twists free from the manager's grip and knees him in the groin to escape confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I twisted my arm free from the manager's grip and kneed him in the groin so I could get away.

grounded_facts: Amy loses her footing while rushing down the stairs, slides several steps, flips over, and lands on her back on a mid-floor landing.
memories.memory_text: I was rushing down the stairs and my feet slipped on the polished steps; I slid several steps, flipped over, and landed on my back on the landing.

grounded_facts: The Manager sees Amy fleeing and shouts for someone to stop her, expressing frustration in his native language.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Manager shout 'Stop her!' and curse at me in his native language while I was fleeing down the stairs, and I knew he wasn't going to chase me himself.

grounded_facts: Amy exits the building abruptly and begins to flee, initially walking calmly when a police car approaches, then accelerating into a run after it passes.
memories.memory_text: I burst out of the building and down the stairs, then forced myself to walk calmly when I saw the police car coming, keeping my eyes down until it passed, and as soon as it did, I started walking faster and then broke into a run.

grounded_facts: From a recorded message, Marla explicitly warns Amy not to open the puzzle box, linking its opening to Winter's victory.
memories.memory_text: I was told not to open the puzzle box—Marla said if I did, Winter would win.

grounded_facts: Marla instructs Amy to go to Pletkow station at midnight, step onto the last car, and find a man named Joey who will guide her.
memories.memory_text: I was told to go to Pletkow station at midnight, step onto the last car, and find a man named Joey who would guide me.

grounded_facts: A private, emotionally charged moment in which Amy watches a pre-recorded video from Marla, who speaks to her from the past with urgent warnings and instructions.
memories.memory_text: I remember Marla sitting in her apartment, speaking directly to me from the past, her voice urgent and sad, warning me about Winter and what was at stake.

grounded_facts: In her final moments on the tape, Marla warns Amy that those she trusts the most should be trusted the least.
memories.memory_text: I heard Marla say, just before she cut the recording, that those I trust the most should be trusted the least.

grounded_facts: Amy inserts and views a videotape left by Marla, receiving urgent instructions and warnings about Winter, the puzzle box, and a mission to save others.
memories.memory_text: I inserted the videotape Marla left for me and watched it play on the TV, sitting there with my drink as the screen filled with snow after it ended.

grounded_facts: After hearing Marla's warning, Amy refrains from opening the puzzle box and places it on the table.
memories.memory_text: I remember Marla warning me not to open the box because if I do, Winter wins — so I set it on the table and told myself not to open it.

grounded_facts: Amy notices an abstract image of a screaming little girl reflected in the puzzle box, which is not present on the TV screen showing static.
memories.memory_text: I noticed an abstract image of a screaming little girl in the reflection of the puzzle box, even though the TV screen only showed static, and I watched it fade as I kept looking.

grounded_facts: Charles voices his fear that Amy's investigative methods may lead to her death and expresses guilt over potentially being responsible.
Charles tells Amy he fears she will get killed due to her methods and doesn't want to feel responsible.
memories.memory_text: I heard Charles tell me he fears I'll get killed because of how I work, and that he doesn't want it to be his fault if it happens—he said it like he was trying to clear his conscience.

grounded_facts: Amy mocks Charles's concern, refuses emotional compromise, and reaffirms her commitment to uncovering the truth.
memories.memory_text: I told Charles I can't do the sensitive thing—he wants me to come home, but I won't back down until I know the truth, so I let him off the hook.

grounded_facts: A phone call between Charles and Amy discussing her investigation and his concerns
memories.memory_text: I remember the phone call with Charles—he woke me, but I was already up working, and he started pressuring me about my methods, saying he didn't want to feel responsible if something happened to me.

grounded_facts: The puzzle box starts to unlock and change shape, emitting light and causing physical disturbances in the room.
memories.memory_text: I was turning the puzzle box in my hands, feeling its edges, when it suddenly started to unlock and change shape—I jumped and set it down. Light came from inside as it clicked into a new form, and the table began to tremble, even the ice in my drink rattling.

grounded_facts: Pinhead manifests behind Amy during the box's transformation but vanishes when interrupted by the phone ringing.
memories.memory_text: I saw a figure—Pinhead—appear behind me in the darkness, but then the phone rang and I startled, hitting the box; when I looked again, he was gone.

grounded_facts: Amy speaks into the phone, rejecting Charles's parental tone and asserting independence.
memories.memory_text: I told Charles I get the message, that he's my editor, not my Mommy, when he started in with that parental tone on the phone.

grounded_facts: Marla's voice comes through the phone with a gurgling, post-mortem warning not to open the box.
Amy answers a call where Marla's voice, distorted and wet, warns her not to open the box before the line dies.
memories.memory_text: I heard Marla's voice come through the phone, gurgling and wet like when she was hanged, telling me not to open the box—and I shoved the phone away from me in fear.

grounded_facts: After the disturbing phone call, Amy stands and pulls her pants on, indicating a decision to exit or prepare for action.
memories.memory_text: I stood up and pulled my pants on after shoving the phone away, ready to get out of that room.

grounded_facts: A subway train arrives at a nearly empty station at night, with unusual conditions including a single door opening and a newspaper-covered car.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the station late at night and saw a strange train pull in, with only one door opening right in front of me, and the car's windows were completely covered in newspaper from the inside.

grounded_facts: Amy asks the conductor if Joey is on the train, indicating her search for a specific person.
memories.memory_text: I asked the conductor if Joey was on the train because I was looking for him.

grounded_facts: The conductor gestures toward the adjoining car and tells Amy to come in, prompting her to board the train.
memories.memory_text: I saw the conductor gesture toward the next car and tell me to come in, so I believed he was letting me board.

grounded_facts: Amy boards a subway car with newspaper-covered windows after being gestured into it by a conductor-like figure, and the train departs.
memories.memory_text: I boarded the newspaper-covered subway car after the conductor told me to come in, and as soon as I got inside, the doors closed and the train started moving.

grounded_facts: Amy shows Joey the Puzzle Box, which causes an immediate and serious reaction.
memories.memory_text: I took the Puzzle Box out of my pack and showed it to Joey. The second he saw it, his expression changed like he'd seen a ghost. He pushed the woman off his lap and became completely serious.

grounded_facts: Joey provides Amy with information about the location where the Deaders can be found, despite his initial hesitation and internal conflict.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Joey that the Deaders hang out near Poteilari and Minvara, on the northeast corner, down a stairway into a closed-up building that's always locked — and that once you get mixed up with them, you might never get loose.

grounded_facts: Joey delivers a final, sincere warning to Amy, urging her to abandon her quest for survival and self-preservation.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Joey to abandon my quest, that I should forget about it, change my name, and become someone different to stay safe.

grounded_facts: Amy rejects Joey's final warning to abandon her search and chooses to proceed toward the Deaders' location.
memories.memory_text: I told Joey I can't back down, that I've got this fucked up thing driving me forward, and I chose to keep going toward the Deaders.

grounded_facts: A clandestine meeting between Amy and Joey takes place in a transformed subway car filled with revelers and drug use, serving as a key intelligence exchange.
memories.memory_text: I moved through the subway car filled with people and drugs, staying focused as I approached Joey. He spotted me, greeted me playfully at first, but everything changed the moment I showed him the Puzzle Box. His demeanor shifted instantly—he became serious, warned me about Poteilari and Minvara, urged me to abandon my mission, even talked about karma. I listened, but I knew I wouldn't stop. I stared at him a moment longer, then left.

grounded_facts: Amy notices a slumped, lone figure in a shiny green raincoat on a bench across the platform, with no visible movement, and approaches it cautiously.
memories.memory_text: I noticed a slumped figure in a shiny green raincoat on the bench across the platform and cautiously moved closer to get a better look.

grounded_facts: Amy observes that the figure has a gray, limp hand hanging off the bench and realizes the person may be dead.
memories.memory_text: I saw that one of the figure's hands was hanging limp off the bench, and it was gray—I realized the person might be dead.

grounded_facts: The seemingly dead figure suddenly opens his eyes and stares at Amy, revealing he is alive despite the pool of blood beneath him.
memories.memory_text: I saw the figure's eyes suddenly pop open and stare at me, those dead-looking black eyes, and I realized he was alive even though there was blood pooling beneath him.

grounded_facts: Winter suddenly appears behind Amy and calls her name, startling her and causing her to stumble.
Winter calls Amy's name from behind, startling her and causing her to stumble and fall to her knees.
memories.memory_text: I heard my name called from behind—'Amy Klein!'—and when I turned, I stumbled forward and fell to my knees, seeing Winter standing there in a black trench coat, staring at me with malevolent eyes.

grounded_facts: As the train arrives, Winter calmly falls backward into its path, seemingly committing suicide or staging a disappearance.
memories.memory_text: I saw Winter calmly fall backward into the path of the arriving train, and I immediately ran toward it, shouting to the driver that someone had fallen in front of the train.

grounded_facts: Amy urgently tells the train driver that someone fell in front of the train, demanding attention and action.
Amy runs to the front of the train and informs the driver that someone fell in front of it.
memories.memory_text: I ran to the front of the train and pounded on the window until the driver opened it, then I shouted at her that somebody fell in front of the train — I needed her to see that this was urgent.

grounded_facts: A tense and surreal event unfolds on a subway platform at night involving a mysterious figure in a green raincoat and Winter's apparent suicide.
memories.memory_text: I saw the train coming in, and then a man fell backward into its path; I ran alongside it and shouted at the driver, but when I looked back, the bench was empty.

grounded_facts: The bench where the man in the green raincoat was sitting is now empty, with no trace of the figure or blood.
memories.memory_text: I looked back and saw that the bench where the man in the green raincoat had been sitting was now empty, with no sign of him or any blood.

grounded_facts: A transit investigation at the train station following Amy's report of a mysterious figure, involving track workers, transit cops, and a driver inspecting the train.

grounded_facts: Amy shoves Marla and screams, blaming her for her condition.
memories.memory_text: I shoved Marla and screamed at her, demanding to know why she did this to me—I had to make her understand I blamed her for my condition.

grounded_facts: Blood soaks through Amy's shirt, and Marla confirms she is dying, just as Marla is.
memories.memory_text: I saw blood soaking through my shirt, and Marla told me I was dying, just like her.

grounded_facts: Marla, as a deceased figure, takes Amy's hand and urges her to leave the train and decide their path.
memories.memory_text: Marla took my hand and pulled me along, urging me to leave the train, and I could hear the panic in her voice as I looked around, unsure.

grounded_facts: Marla Chen, visibly decaying, appears on the train and urges Amy to leave, claiming she is dying like Marla.
memories.memory_text: I saw Marla, decaying and desperate, grab my hand and urge me to leave, telling me she’s dying just like I am—I realized then she wasn’t helping me out of strength, but from her own failing will.

grounded_facts: Amy expresses desire to go home, and Marla agrees to take her, initiating their departure from the train station.
memories.memory_text: I said I just wanted to go home, and Marla agreed, saying, 'Then let's go home,' and we started to leave the station together.

grounded_facts: A surreal journey on a train populated by the dead, serving as a liminal space between life and death.
memories.memory_text: I remember stumbling through the train full of celebrants, then running into Marla Chen—her decaying body shocked me—and we jumped down to an abandoned track and walked into the darkness, though I'm not sure what it all means.

grounded_facts: Marla discloses that she attempted suicide by hanging and was revived by Winter, marking a turning point in her psychological state and commitment to the group's ideology.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Marla that she had attempted suicide by hanging and was revived by Winter, and that everyone celebrated her revival as if it were a rebirth.

grounded_facts: A tense nighttime walk through a distorted subway tunnel where Marla imparts key ideological and personal revelations to Amy while moving toward an unknown destination.
memories.memory_text: I remember walking quickly with Marla through a strange, twisting subway tunnel lit by eerie blue lights, pipes overhead dripping water and hissing steam, moving forward into the unknown.

grounded_facts: Marla states that true acceptance requires self-inflicted violence, not just harm from others, framing it as a necessary step before giving one's soul willingly.
memories.memory_text: I remember Marla telling me that true acceptance means being able to harm myself, not just letting others hurt me — that it's the final step before giving my soul willingly.

grounded_facts: Marla tells Amy that the group's leader promises an eternal paradise of ultimate pleasures, contingent on the absence of fear and doubt.
memories.memory_text: I heard from Marla that the group's leader promises an eternal paradise of ultimate pleasures, but only if we have no fear or doubts.

grounded_facts: Marla claims that fear is essential for growth within the group's philosophy, reinforcing the idea that there is no return without external intervention.
memories.memory_text: I remember Marla telling me that fear is where you go to learn, and then saying I couldn't turn back—only Winter could bring me back.

grounded_facts: Winter appears as a savior figure, calling Amy by name and declaring 'All roads lead home,' asserting his control and offering emotional resolution.
Winter appears dramatically as a train approaches, calling out to Amy with the phrase 'All roads lead home,' halting the forward momentum of the scene and redirecting Amy's attention.
memories.memory_text: I heard Winter call my name as the train roared toward us, and when I turned, he was there with his arms open, saying 'All roads lead home,' pulling my attention away from the track and from Marla.

grounded_facts: Amy regains consciousness in a psychiatric hospital bed, discovering she is physically restrained with leather straps and under observation.
memories.memory_text: I woke up in a hospital bed with white sheets, and when I tried to move, I realized I was tied down with leather straps—my hands and legs were restrained, and I could see Charles watching me from a chair while the curtain was pulled closed around me.

grounded_facts: Amy is hospitalized in a psychiatric ward following a severe mental breakdown characterized by physical collapse and extreme behavior.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Charles that I had a psychotic episode, a major mental breakdown, and that I'd been tied down for a day and a half.

grounded_facts: Charles informs Amy that Marla Chen was found dead, having hanged herself, likely after sending them the tape.
memories.memory_text: I heard Charles tell me that they found Marla dead in her room, that she had hanged herself, probably right after sending us the tape, and I asked if he meant the police found her.

grounded_facts: Charles delivers news in a flippant, media-obsessed tone, reframing Amy's trauma as potential story material.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Charles that this could be a good story, with titles like 'Psychotic - Episode One' or 'Psychotic Pilot Episode,' and he joked about me taking notes with a felt-tip pen, all while speaking in that flippant way that made me feel like my pain was just material to him.

grounded_facts: Orderly Kircher makes a pun about Amy being 'bound' to get hurt, referencing her physical restraints with inappropriate humor.
memories.memory_text: I heard Orderly Kircher make a joke about me being 'bound to get hurt' because of the restraints, and I told him not to quit his day job.

grounded_facts: Charles whispers to Amy about arranging a camera in the hospital, indicating an intent to document her condition for professional use.
memories.memory_text: Charles leaned in and whispered to me that he'd see about getting a camera in here, like he wanted to document everything.

grounded_facts: After Charles leaves, Amy checks for staff and exits the bed, defying her physical restraints and hospital protocol.
memories.memory_text: After Charles left, I watched him go, waited a moment, then hopped out of bed. I looked around to make sure no nurses or orderlies were nearby before I stepped out of frame.

grounded_facts: Amy approaches a little girl drawing alone in the corner; the girl draws a disturbing image of Amy as a Cenobite, leading to a moment of supernatural revelation.
The Little Girl draws Amy's face as a Cenobite, claiming she only draws what she sees, thereby confronting Amy with a terrifying vision of her transformed self.
The Little Girl reveals a drawing depicting Amy's face transformed into a Cenobite, causing Amy to experience terror and realize the supernatural accuracy of the image.
memories.memory_text: I approached a little girl drawing alone in the corner, and when I asked if I could join her, she showed me a drawing of my own face twisted into a Cenobite—with dark empty eyes and a knife wound in my chest—and said, 'I only draw what I see, Amy,' which made me feel a surge of terror as I realized the image felt supernaturally true.

grounded_facts: Marla subtly informs Amy that she is the person Winter has been searching for — the one with the right soul to solve the puzzle — increasing Amy's sense of destiny and danger.
memories.memory_text: I remember Marla telling me I'm the one Winter's been searching for — the only one with the right soul to solve the puzzle, a mix of depravity and loneliness.

grounded_facts: Marla emphasizes that Winter must be present for Amy to return, framing him as both threat and key to her survival.
memories.memory_text: I was told Winter has to be there for me to come back — he's the key, but also the threat, just like he was for all the others.

grounded_facts: Amy encounters Marla in the psych ward, who cryptically reveals that Amy is the chosen one destined to solve the puzzle Winter seeks, warning her of limited time and the necessity of facing inner truths.
memories.memory_text: I encountered Marla in the psych ward, and though she first acted like she didn’t know me, she leaned in and told me I’m the chosen one destined to solve a puzzle Winter can’t, warning me that time is short and I must face the truth hidden within me if I ever want to be free.

grounded_facts: Blood begins to soak through Amy's hospital gown at the site of her previous injury, signaling physical deterioration or supernatural manifestation.
memories.memory_text: I saw blood starting to soak through my hospital gown where my wound was, and I could feel my strength fading.

grounded_facts: Marla informs Amy that she is the chosen one capable of solving the puzzle that Winter seeks, warning her that time is running out and that Winter must be present for her return.
memories.memory_text: I heard Marla warn me that I'm the chosen one who must solve the puzzle, that time is running out, and Winter must be present for me to return.

grounded_facts: After delivering her warning, Marla disappears along with all other patients, leaving the ward completely empty and silent, suggesting a shift between reality and illusion.
memories.memory_text: After Marla gave her warning, I looked up and she was gone — everyone was gone — and the ward was completely empty and silent.

grounded_facts: The walls of the corridor gradually turn white as Amy walks down it, symbolizing a shift in the environment or her psychological state.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the walls around me gradually turning white with each step I took, as if the corridor was bleaching out.

grounded_facts: Amy observes blood draining from her wound, indicating physical change or possible unreality.
memories.memory_text: I looked down and saw blood draining from my wound, which made me realize something was changing in my body.

grounded_facts: Amy hears a faint, echoing scream from a little girl, prompting her movement and emotional response.
memories.memory_text: I heard a faint, echoing scream from a little girl—familiar and urgent—and I turned back down the corridor, stumbling as I moved toward her voice.

grounded_facts: Amy hears a door banging and rattling, suggesting someone is trying to escape.
memories.memory_text: I heard a door banging and rattling, like someone was fighting to get out.

grounded_facts: Amy's father looks in her direction but behaves as if he does not see her, creating emotional distance.
memories.memory_text: I saw my father look down the hallway toward me, but he didn't acknowledge me, like I wasn't even there.

grounded_facts: Amy becomes visibly weaker, stumbling as she walks, with glazing eyes and blurred vision indicating declining physical condition.
memories.memory_text: I could feel myself getting weaker with every step, stumbling as I walked, and then my vision started to blur as my eyes began to glaze over.

grounded_facts: Amy notices a trail of bright red blood behind her on the white floor, making her aware of the severity of her injury.
memories.memory_text: I looked down and saw a trail of bright red blood behind me on the white floor, and that's when I realized how bad my injury really was.

grounded_facts: The father moves toward the rattling closet door with growing rage, responding to Young Amy's screams from inside.
memories.memory_text: I was screaming from inside the closet as my father marched toward it, his rage building, and I could tell he was coming for me.

grounded_facts: Amy shouts a command to leave someone alone, indicating protective or defensive behavior toward a female third party.
memories.memory_text: I shouted 'Leave her alone!' to stop someone from hurting her.

grounded_facts: Young Amy violently stabs the father in the chest with a butcher knife during a confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I stabbed my father in the chest with the butcher knife as soon as he opened the door.

grounded_facts: Amy's Father collapses after being stabbed in the chest with a knife, dying as his head falls backward.
memories.memory_text: I saw my Father fall backward with the knife buried in his chest, and I watched his head drop back as he died.

grounded_facts: Amy collapses to her knees and her head falls to the floor as she loses consciousness due to her injuries.
memories.memory_text: I hit my knees and tried to hold on, but I couldn't stay up—my head fell back and everything went dark as I passed out from the pain.

grounded_facts: A vision or apparition of Young Amy appears at the scene, standing over the body and smiling for the first time.
memories.memory_text: I appeared at the scene as a vision, standing alone over the body, and for the first time, I smiled.

grounded_facts: A ritual conducted by the Deaders to open the puzzle box and summon the Cenobites, culminating in supernatural consequences.
memories.memory_text: I remember waking up on that mattress surrounded by the Deaders, all chanting as I saw the puzzle box on the altar glowing with rays of light, and a black void forming behind them.

grounded_facts: Winter insists Amy complete the ritual, claiming she is 'one of us now'.
memories.memory_text: Winter kept telling me I was one of them now and insisted I say the words and complete the ritual with them.

grounded_facts: Amy refuses to complete the ritual by stabbing the knife into the altar, defying Winter's command.
memories.memory_text: I refused to do what Winter wanted, so I took the knife and slammed it into the altar beside me.

grounded_facts: Pinhead steps through the void into the world, followed by Cenobites, marking the full opening of the portal.
memories.memory_text: I saw Pinhead step through the void into our world, and I stumbled back in fear as he approached Winter.

grounded_facts: Pinhead asserts that Winter misunderstood the nature of the puzzle box and his place in its power structure.
memories.memory_text: I heard Pinhead tell Winter that he misunderstood the puzzle box and that there's no way in but through him.

grounded_facts: Pinhead declares that Amy belongs to him because she opened the box.
memories.memory_text: I remember Pinhead telling me that I belong to him because I opened the box and brought them all together, that it was my choice and now I have to pay the price by giving myself to him like the others did.

grounded_facts: Marla, near death, tells Amy that only she can stop the ritual by not giving her soul willingly.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Marla, as she was dying, that only I could stop the ritual by not giving my soul willingly, and I understood then that I had to choose death over surrender.

grounded_facts: Pinhead has Winter torn apart by hooks and chains as punishment for claiming ownership of the puzzle box.
memories.memory_text: I watched as hooks and chains tore Winter apart, and I saw the meat hanging from them — I realized then what I had to do and raised my knife.

grounded_facts: Amy reverses the Deader chant, affirming reality and rejecting the illusion of unreality.
Amy reverses the Deader chant, affirming the reality of her body and senses to break the ritual.
memories.memory_text: I reversed the Deader chant, declaring that my skin is real, my eyes are real, and my muscles are real, affirming the truth of my body and senses to break the ritual.

grounded_facts: Amy stabs herself in the chest to deny her soul to Pinhead, choosing death over damnation.
memories.memory_text: I stabbed myself in the chest with the knife to deny my soul to Pinhead, choosing to die rather than let him claim me.

grounded_facts: The Cenobites, including Pinhead, are sucked back into the void as the puzzle box closes.
memories.memory_text: I saw Pinhead and the other Cenobites get sucked back into the void as the puzzle box closed.

memories.memory_text: I slipped the tape recorder into my coat pocket and turned it on, watching them through half-lidded eyes while pretending to come down hard on X—I even faked the tremors, the glazed look, let him think I swallowed it before flicking the pill away when he turned.

After everyone left, the room turned heavy and quiet—he pulled me onto the mattress, his hands tearing at my clothes, and my vision started swimming like the walls were breathing; I couldn’t push him off, and then suddenly he went limp, passed out on top of me.
I walked into Charles’s office and he didn’t even turn around—just mocked me with that stupid comment about patchouli oil and sweat, like I was some predictable cliché.

I picked up the cassette recorder and started to defend myself about the crack whore story, but it felt hollow—like he already knew I hadn’t delivered, and this was just another performance in our messed-up history.

I reached between the mattress and the box spring and pulled out a small red photo folder—dusty, like it had been hidden for a while. When I opened it, the first pictures were of another 'deader' party, and then I saw Marla smiling in one, alive, like she was still here.

I turned to a photo where Winter stood next to Marla, holding something, and then the next image showed a noose in the frame, rope dangling right in front of her face—she was smiling, but it looked wrong, forced. I couldn't tell if someone was standing in the shadows behind them, but I felt like I was being watched just looking at it.

I pushed the tape in with my toe because I couldn't make myself touch it, and when Marla’s face came on screen—tired, scared, talking like she was already gone—I felt the ice pack slip down my arm, melting. She told me not to open the box, but then she told me to go to Pletkow station, to find Joey, to save them… like I was the only one left who could.

I saw a man in a shiny green raincoat slumped on a bench, and when I got closer, his dead black eyes snapped open—there was blood pooling under him, and I froze, my heel slipping off the platform edge.

I saw a figure in a green raincoat on the bench. As I got closer, the hand was limp and gray. His eyes opened—black, lifeless. Then I heard someone call my name. I turned and saw Winter on the edge, staring. The train came in. He fell backward into its path. I ran, screaming to the driver, but there was no one. The bench was empty.

I remember standing in the rain with Charles under his umbrella, asking him why he gave me the story, and needing to say it out loud—'It's real—or I'm crazy'—because I couldn't keep pretending the things I saw weren't happening.

I remember him calling me a glutton for knowledge, saying I eat what he's too afraid to touch—like I'm his hunger made flesh—and then realizing, with a chill, that he meant it as a compliment, that he needs me because I don't stop, even when I should.

I remember sitting across from Winter, my hands unsteady as I placed the Puzzle Box on the table—when he said he chose me, not by accident, but like I was meant to be here, and his smile made my skin crawl.
He leaned in close and said I was already on the train and couldn't get off. He told me I was in more danger than I could imagine.
I felt my hand shaking in his grip, and his words about it being an absence, less than nothing, started to sink in—I could feel myself slipping, like I was losing hold of myself.
I saw Winter holding that knife out to me, calm like it meant nothing, and for a second I almost reached for it—then I realized what he was offering and shoved myself backward, heart slamming.
They started chanting, hands grabbing at me from all sides, their voices droning—'my skin isn't real'—and I screamed 'No!' as I fought to pull away, limbs flailing, trying to break free.
I remember gripping the puzzle box, turning it in my hands while Charles tried to talk me out of the story—he said it was too dangerous, but I told him this was the one I was born to write.

I was standing there, shaking, trying to call 999 with blood all over my hands, and when the line picked up, it wasn't an operator—it was that gurgling sound again, Marla's voice, saying 'Only he can bring you back' like it was some kind of message meant just for me.

After I ripped the phone out, I turned and saw him—Pinhead—just standing there, calmly reading Walt Whitman from a book on the shelf like he belonged, then saying he liked my taste in books as if this was normal, as if he hadn't just appeared out of nowhere.
I saw that man picking crickets off the wall and chewing them—so slow, so blank—and then he offered me one, smiling like it was normal. I didn’t even think, I just leapt back and ran.
I heard the rumble from below and scrambled toward it—then threw myself down on a subway grate, feeling the hot air rise. When I saw the entrance above, I knew I could get away.

I pulled open my shirt right in front of Joey, tore the tape down my chest—blood smeared under my fingers when I wiped it away. I needed him to see it, to tell me why I was still feeling this pain if I wasn’t even alive.

Joey just sat there, pale under the flashing lights, and said life and death aren’t that different—like it meant something. I don’t know if I believed him, but the way he looked at me… like he already knew I didn’t belong here, or that I never would.

Marla’s voice cracked as she told me she’d tried to hang herself, that Winter brought her back, and that real transcendence only comes when you’re ready to destroy yourself willingly—I saw the yellow tears in her eyes and felt the ground shake beneath us.

I turned toward the roaring train, then back to Marla—just as Winter appeared in front of us with arms wide open, screaming 'All roads lead home' over the noise, and I froze, unsure if he was salvation or danger.
I woke up and couldn't move—my hands and legs were strapped down with thick leather belts, and all I could see was a white curtain closed around me like a cage.
Charles told me I was found on the floor covered in bodily fluids, and when he said that, I remembered the blood—but then I looked down and my gown was clean, no stain at all.

The little girl showed me a drawing—my face twisted into a Cenobite, empty eyes, skin pulled back with hooks around a knife wound in my chest. She said, 'I only draw what I see... Amy,' and I felt my breath stop.
I saw Marla sitting across the room—alive, whole—but when I called her name, she whispered that Winter was watching, that this place was for troublemakers, and he was trying to make us believe.
I heard that scream—faint, echoing—and when I turned back down the corridor, the walls started to change, bleaching white with every step I took.
I looked down and saw the blood draining from my wound—then I stumbled back, hearing violent banging on a door, like someone trapped, fighting to get out.
I saw my father look right at me, but he didn't react—he just turned and walked away. I didn't think, I just followed.
I followed my father down the hallway. He opened the door to his office and went in. I stepped in behind him.
I was screaming inside the closet, my hands pressed against the door as it shook—I could hear him coming, his footsteps getting louder, and I knew he wasn’t going to stop this time.

I remember the way his hand tightened on the doorknob, how he raised his arm to hit me—but then I saw the knife in my hand, and I just... made it stop. I buried it in his chest before he could take another step.

I screamed and tried to hold on, but everything was slowing down—my knees hit the floor, and I couldn't keep my head up. The last thing I saw was my father falling, the knife in his chest, and then nothing.
I was standing there—me, but not me—just watching, feeling nothing. I saw the body on the floor and then I smiled, cold and quiet, like it meant nothing.

I opened my eyes and saw the Deaders all around me chanting, their voices hollow, and then I saw the puzzle box on the altar—solved—waiting, like it was alive. Winter stood at my feet holding out the stiletto, and for a second, I felt something like relief as I reached for it.

I remember my hand closing around the stiletto, the metal cold and real—too real—and then I knew I couldn't do it. I slammed the knife into the altar, not into flesh, and the air cracked like something broke open.
I left everything behind—my clothes, my money, just vanished like Marla Chen. I don’t know how I got here or why I’m not dead, but I can still feel the static, like it’s pulling me somewhere.

memories.memory_text: I hear my name spoken at the door, called out by someone claiming to be family—half-sister, same mother—but I can’t see her, only feel the weight of that lie hanging in the air as the key turns.
I felt the lace bite into my neck as I leaned forward, the pipe cold against the taut strand, my body already heavy, the flies gathering even before the breath left me.
I stared into the camera, my hands trembling, and told Amy not to open the box—because if she does, Winter wins. I could hear him coming, but I had to make her understand.

I told Amy to go to Pletkow station at midnight, to the south end of the platform, step onto the last car, and find a man named Joey. I said to tell him I sent her. I shut off the camera before Winter broke in.
I reached through the phone, my voice a wet choke, and I said it—'Don't open...'—just before the silence took me again.
I told Amy Klein to find Joey, to say my name—that it would open the door. I don’t know if it was a warning or a betrayal, only that the path had to be walked.
I left the Puzzle Box behind in the bathroom, and I warned Amy about it—about him—knowing she’d find it, knowing she’d come this far.

I whispered through the phone line, 'Only he can bring you back,' knowing she'd hear it—knowing it was the only way to reach her without being seen. Then I tore the cord from the wall, my hands trembling, not sure if I was helping or just pulling her deeper in.

I remember grabbing Amy’s hand, feeling how warm it was compared to my rotting fingers, and begging her to move — I had to get her to choose, but I didn’t even know if I could help her the way I was supposed to.

I told Amy I put my head through a noose and jumped—ten feet down. They cut me down, Winter breathed into me, and I was alive… but it didn’t fix anything. I could feel the rope giving way beneath me, and then the fall—just like that, the tightrope snapped.

I told her fear is where you go to learn—just before the train roared in. I meant it. I whispered that surrender, doing it to yourself, is the only way to give your soul willingly. But I could see she didn’t understand yet.
I leaned in close and whispered to Amy that Winter is watching us, feeling the weight of his unseen eyes in this place meant for breaking people like us.
I poked Amy's chest where the wound would be and told her the puzzle is inside her — I saw the fear in her eyes and knew she still didn't understand, but she will.
It's all about finding the truth... I said it into the silence, hoping she'd hear it not just in her ears but in her bones.
I remember the chanting, the heat in the room, and seeing that solved Puzzle Box on the altar—Amy reaching for the knife like she finally understood what it meant to give in.
I left everything behind—my clothes, my money, the life I was pretending to live—and vanished like Marla Chen, no trace, just silence where I used to be.

I felt the walls close in around me, so tight I couldn't bring my hands together—had to pass the lighter over my head, and when it slipped, the dark swallowed everything.

I held my ground and told Amy to finish it, my voice cutting through the chaos—she had to say the words, she had to complete the ritual, it was the only way forward.
I looked Pinhead in the face and told him it was mine—that the box belonged to me—knowing he would try to take it, but refusing to yield, even as the air changed and the moment cracked open.
